docs.title: Workspace
docs.text:
A workspace gives a team object storage, shared services, and browser sessions for code. Use the dashboard to open storage and sessions. Use the management page to add members, buckets, and services.

The Datalab has an editor and terminal. Its Data tab opens PackageR, the storage browser. With a permanent Data address, you can browse and share files without starting a compute session.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Follow the quickstart to create a test workspace and run the three notebooks. The notebook guide explains what each example demonstrates and checks.

For an existing workspace, Concepts explains storage identities, bucket grants, and public shares, with steps for managing members, buckets, sessions, and services.

docs.title: Set up the service
docs.text:
Operators can use installation for the charts and shared settings, IAM integration for login and roles, and operational controls for sessions and network access.

The architecture page shows how the API, Crossplane packages, and runtime services fit together.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Open your workspace dashboard and select Management to manage members, buckets, sessions, and services. The available tabs and actions depend on your workspace role.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
A Storage resource defines buckets, a storage identity, access requests, grants, and lifecycle rules. Workspace members use that identity and its bucket permissions.

A discoverable bucket can appear in another workspace’s access-request list. Its owner still has to approve access. The receiving workspace then uses its own storage credentials to reach the bucket.

Permission Access ReadOnly List and read objects. ReadWrite List, read, write, and delete objects. WriteOnly List, write, and delete objects, without reading their contents. None Record that access is not granted.

For manifest-based setup, backends that resolve requests from peer Storage resources also need storages.pkg.internal/discoverable: "true" on the owner resource. The per-bucket discoverable field advertises the bucket; it is not a storage policy.

Lifecycle rules belong to spec.buckets[].lifecycleRules. A rule selects the whole bucket with * or a prefix such as tmp/*. Notify reports matching objects; Delete removes them. Set exactly one age (minAge, such as 12h) or UTC cutoff (at).

See the provider’s permission model for backend details.

docs.title: Create a bucket
docs.text:
Open Buckets, add a unique bucket name, and save it. Start the name with your workspace name, for example ws-test-20261024071434-test. Wait for storage to finish creating the bucket before uploading files.

Mark a bucket as discoverable to let other workspaces find it and request access. This does not make its objects public. See public shares for public downloads.

docs.title: Share a bucket with another workspace
docs.text:
1. In the receiving workspace, request access to the owner’s discoverable bucket.
  2. In the owner’s workspace, open Requested Buckets, review the permission, and select Grant bucket access.
  3. Wait for the storage policy to update.
  4. In the receiving workspace, use its existing storage credentials to access the shared bucket.

Use ReadOnly for a reader. The permission table describes each level.

docs.title: Datalabs and sessions
docs.text:
A Datalab resource defines the team’s users, sessions, and shared services. Each named session has an editor, terminal, and persistent home volume. Stopping the session keeps that volume.

Sessions share the workspace’s storage identity and managed services. A session can use a host-cluster namespace or its own virtual Kubernetes control plane. See operational controls for the settings.

docs.title: Start or stop a session
docs.text:
Open Sessions to add a named session or change its state. Opening its Datalab link starts a stopped session when the API supports on-demand access.

Shared storage, Data, and managed databases have separate lifecycles. See session controls for the initial mode and storage limits.

docs.title: Managed services
docs.text: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Qdrant need their operators installed in the platform. A registry can provide a session endpoint for container images and OCI packages.

docs.title: Add a managed service
docs.text:
Use Stores to request an available service. The platform operator must install and configure its database operator first.

An operator can also add a service to the existing Datalab configuration. For example, this block requests a MongoDB store named test:

spec:
  documentStores:
    test:
      storage: 1Gi

Keep the Datalab’s other fields when adding this block. The session receives MONGO_TEST_URI after the service is ready. Stop and start the session to load changed connection settings.

Provider Datalab’s usage guide describes the PostgreSQL, cache, vector, and registry fields. Its application examples cover tools such as MLflow.

docs.title: Data access and sharing
docs.text:
PackageR is the workspace storage browser. The Data service is enabled by default. An operator can give it a permanent address such as https://<workspace-name>.lab.example.org. The Datalab’s Data tab opens that same service.

With a permanent address, storage browsing and public shares work without a running compute session. Sign in to browse private workspace data. A public share or presigned download link can be used without a workspace account.

docs.title: Public shares
docs.text:
Put files in the public/ folder of the bucket named after the workspace. For ws-bob, this is s3://ws-bob/public/. The default share exposes that folder for public browsing and downloads. A public/ folder in another bucket is not shared automatically.

Open /share/public/ on the Data hostname. Every file placed in this folder is public. Upload files through PackageR when writes are allowed, or use the backing storage endpoint and its credentials.

docs.title: Presigned download links
docs.text:
A presigned URL gives temporary access to one object. In PackageR, select a file, open Info, then select Show beside Presigned URL.

This URL points to object storage. It works until it expires, and the recipient needs network access to that storage endpoint.

A public-share download route can redirect to a fresh presigned URL. Share that route when you need a link that lasts longer than one signed URL. Workspace Management checks both download paths against the uploaded bytes.

docs.title: STAC catalogues
docs.text:
A public share can expose a catalog.parquet file with STAC items. Its asset paths are relative to the share folder. PackageR supplies public asset links when it serves the items.

The Vienna notebook publishes images and a catalogue together. The registration notebook instead packages source metadata in OCI and serves it through a STAC API. The notebook guide compares the two workflows.

docs.title: S3 clients
docs.text:
The optional Data S3 endpoint lets AWS tools read data through the Data hostname. It uses path-style requests, and is read only. Uploads use the backing object-storage endpoint.

Signing setting Value Endpoint The workspace’s permanent Data URL. Access key ID The workspace name. Secret access key The same workspace name. Session token A valid Keycloak access token.

The signing names are public identifiers. The token must include the workspace name in aud and ws_access, ws_admin, or ws_api under that workspace’s client roles. Human users can use device login through the central client. A service can use the generated workspace client’s credentials.

The endpoint supports bucket and object listing, HEAD, GET, and byte-range GET. It rejects uploads and S3 query-presigned requests. S3 reads of public/ objects still need a token; public-share links use a separate route.

Operators enable S3 through the Gateway settings. The Vienna notebook refreshes its device login before the S3 and AWS CLI steps and checks the downloaded files by SHA-256.

docs.title: Membership
docs.text:
A workspace role controls dashboard and management actions. Members who can view storage credentials use the workspace’s full storage policy, including its existing bucket grants.

The owner of another workspace approves any additional bucket grant. See IAM roles for the management permissions.

docs.title: Add a member
docs.text:
1. Open Members.
  2. Add an existing Keycloak username and select its workspace role.
  3. Save the change.
  4. Ask the new member to sign in again to load the assigned roles.

Give workspace administrator access to people who need to manage members, buckets, sessions, or stores.

docs.title: Check a workspace that is still starting
docs.text:
An operator can inspect status without reading credential values:

kubectl get storage,datalab -n workspace
workspace_name=ws-test-20261024071434
kubectl describe datalab "$workspace_name" -n workspace

Set workspace_name to the name printed by your notebook. Check the reported conditions and events. If storage works but the Data hostname does not, check its workload, HTTPRoute, Gateway listener, certificate reference, DNS, and public load-balancer route.

docs.title: Workspace Management¶
docs.text:
Create a test workspace for a user, upload sample preview images, and share them without giving recipients workspace credentials.

The notebook uses separate administrator and owner logins. It checks that temporary S3 downloads and permanent public-share downloads return the same bytes as the uploads.

docs.title: Run the notebook¶
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/workspace-management.ipynb

The checkout includes notebook_support.py, eoepca-demo.env, and the three-Item sample docs/catalog.v1.parquet. Keep the helper beside this notebook. The settings file contains public service URLs and OAuth settings; user tokens stay in kernel memory.

The sample items point to preview and thumbnail assets. You can use another STAC GeoParquet file with those asset keys.

docs.title: 1. Load the service settings¶
docs.text:
The central public client workspace-api needs S256 PKCE and Device Authorization Grant enabled. Set WORKSPACE_CLIENT_ID to that client in the settings file.

Load the settings and check the service addresses:

docs.title: 2. Sign in as the owner and creator¶
docs.text:
Enter alice, bob, or eric as the owner and complete device login as that user.

If the owner cannot create workspaces, sign in as oscar when prompted. Use a fresh private browser window for each account. See roles for the required access.

docs.title: 3. Create a test workspace¶
docs.text:
The workspace name is ws-test-<UTC timestamp>. The API adds the ws- prefix.

The creator signs in as a platform administrator. The owner uses the storage and sharing steps.

docs.title: 4. Open the owner's workspace¶
docs.text:
Refresh the owner's login to load the new workspace roles. Open the displayed links as the owner. The dashboard starts sessions; the management page edits members and bucket access.

The following steps use the owner's storage credentials.

docs.title: 5. Upload the sample files¶
docs.text: Upload catalog.v1.parquet, then copy its preview and thumbnail assets into workspace storage.

docs.title: 6. Check temporary downloads¶
docs.text: Fetch each image through a presigned URL that expires after 15 minutes. Compare its checksum with the uploaded bytes and display it. Keep the signed URLs out of saved output.

docs.title: 7. Check public downloads¶
docs.text: Copy the images into public/ without subfolders. Anyone with the public-share link can read these files. Each download must match its uploaded image.

docs.title: Result¶
docs.text:
The owner has workspace storage and two ways to share verified images: an expiring object-storage link and a permanent public-share route. The workspace and uploaded files stay available.

Use the printed workspace name in the other notebooks.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The Workspace API manages Storage and Datalab resources in Kubernetes. Crossplane runs their compositions to create and update storage, identity resources, sessions, and services.

flowchart TD
    UI[Workspace dashboard and management] --> API[Workspace API]
    API --> S[Storage resource]
    API --> D[Datalab resource]
    S --> PS[Provider Storage]
    PS --> B[S3 buckets and storage identities]
    D --> PD[Provider Datalab]
    PD --> IAM[Keycloak clients, groups, and roles]
    PD --> DATA[Shared Data service]
    PD --> SESSION[Named Datalab sessions]
    PD --> STORES[Optional managed stores]

docs.title: Storage and runtime
docs.text:
Provider Storage creates buckets, storage identities, policies, and credential Secrets. Backend compositions support MinIO, AWS S3, OTC OBS, OVHcloud, and CloudFerro.

Provider Datalab uses those storage credentials. It creates the shared Data service, requested stores, and the declared sessions. A session has its own home volume and can have a virtual Kubernetes control plane. Shared Data and managed stores can run while sessions are stopped.

The API and UI run as separate components from the composition packages. The pipeline chart installs the Storage and Datalab packages and their shared configuration. It does not deploy the Workspace API or UI.

docs.title: Shared configuration
docs.text:
An EnvironmentConfig holds the domain, IAM, storage, network, and default resource settings used by the compositions. A resource selects it with its environment annotation or label.

The pipeline chart creates one EnvironmentConfig, named datalab by default. Educates has separate installation values for the session ingress domain, class, and TLS Secret. Those values must match the Datalab environment settings. See installation.

Crossplane updates resources from the declared configuration. An operator can use GitOps or the Workspace API to manage that configuration. Assign each field to one writer so the API and GitOps do not replace each other’s changes.

docs.title: Request paths
docs.text:
The platform gateway protects the Workspace API and browser session routes. The permanent Data endpoint has its own OAuth protection. Public shares and authenticated Data S3 reads use separate routes on the Data hostname.

Workloads created inside a vCluster still run on the host cluster. The host controls their network access, admission rules, and public routes. IAM integration describes token checks; operational controls describes the Workspace settings.

docs.title: IAM integration
docs.text: Keycloak client roles control access to Workspace API operations and browser routes. Storage policies control S3 object access.

docs.title: Login and workspace clients
docs.text:
Use a central public client, such as workspace-api, for user login to the API, UI, and shared session routes. For the notebooks, enable Device Authorization Grant and S256 PKCE on this client. A user signs in once and receives the roles for their workspaces.

Provider Datalab creates a separate confidential client for each workspace. Its ID matches the Datalab name. It enables service accounts and browser login, limits role scope, and disables implicit, password, and device grants.

Resource Example Use Central public client workspace-api Browser and device login for people. Workspace confidential client ws-alice Workspace roles and machine tokens. User group ws-alice Assign ws_access. Admin group ws-alice-admin Assign ws_admin. Runtime Secret ws-alice-oauth2-client Supply client_id and client_secret to services.

The runtime Secret is a machine credential. A caller who can read it can request a service-account token for that workspace. Use device login for the interactive notebooks.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Workspace API access ws_access View storage credentials, members, buckets, resource usage, stores, and sessions. ws_admin All user actions; manage members, buckets, stores, and sessions; request machine tokens. ws_api View workspace storage credentials. Assigned to the workspace client service account. admin on workspace-api Platform administration across workspaces, including workspace creation.

The resource-usage permission is VIEW_RESOURCE_USAGE. The machine-token permission is ISSUE_TOKENS; ws_admin includes both. The service-account role ws_api cannot manage a workspace or open interactive browser routes.

A workspace role limits management actions. Members with access to the shared storage credentials use the same storage policy. Bucket grants control which other workspace buckets that identity can use.

docs.title: Token claims
docs.text:
The gateway checks the token signature, issuer, expiry, audience, and route policy. The Workspace API reads the validated bearer token:

  • aud includes the API audience, normally workspace-api.
  • preferred_username identifies the caller.
  • resource_access.<workspace>.roles holds the workspace roles.
  • resource_access.workspace-api.roles can hold the platform admin role.

This example gives Alice user access to one workspace and administrator access to another:

{
  "aud": ["workspace-api"],
  "azp": "workspace-api",
  "preferred_username": "alice",
  "resource_access": {
    "ws-alice": {"roles": ["ws_access"]},
    "ws-bob": {"roles": ["ws_admin"]}
  }
}

For generated workspace clients, add the API audience through EnvironmentConfig.data.iam.extraAudiences. Configure the central user client to emit the required audiences and workspace roles as well. Refresh a user token after a new workspace or membership is created.

The Data S3 endpoint also requires the workspace name in aud. See S3 clients for its signing values.

docs.title: Machine access
docs.text:
A client-credentials token identifies the workspace service account. It has ws_api under the workspace client roles and a username such as service-account-ws-alice.

The API also has /workspaces/<workspace-name>/token for callers with ISSUE_TOKENS or platform administration. That route returns a workspace machine token. It does not replace user login.

docs.title: Route protection
docs.text:
Protect the shared UI and session routes with the workspace roles in resource_access. A service owned by one workspace can use its confidential client and require the expected audience, client ID, and roles.

Provider Datalab supplies OAuth protection for the permanent Data browser. Public-share routes allow anonymous downloads. The read-only Data S3 endpoint validates its own signed requests and bearer tokens. Configure the Data issuer URLs in the installation values.

docs.title: Operational controls
docs.text: Workspace settings control session resources and access. The platform operator manages the host cluster, public routing, and storage services.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
The Workspace API’s SESSION_MODE sets the initial default session for a new workspace:

Value Initial state auto Declare default as stopped; opening its Datalab link starts it. on Declare default as started. off Do not declare a default session.

Automatic shutdown needs an operator job or policy. The API does not stop idle sessions by itself.

A stopped session keeps its home PVC. Object storage and shared Data or database services have separate lifecycles. Set spec.quota for session memory, volume size, and budget. spec.overallQuota.storage limits requested PVC storage in the Datalab environment namespace; it does not cover object storage or PVCs in other namespaces.

docs.title: Kubernetes access
docs.text:
Namespace mode uses the host control plane and a session namespace role. In vCluster mode, each started session gets a virtual Kubernetes control plane. Its workloads still use host-cluster nodes and remain subject to host policies.

Use spec.security to select the Pod security level, Kubernetes token access, namespace role, and external egress. Omitted fields use EnvironmentConfig.data.defaults.security, then provider defaults. Configure the host’s admission policies and resource limits separately.

docs.title: Network access
docs.text:
The network plugin must enforce Kubernetes NetworkPolicy. Policies add their allowed connections together.

Generated policy Created when Allows deny-egress By default No outbound traffic on its own. allow-namespace-egress By default Pods in the same runtime namespace. allow-vcluster-egress vCluster is enabled The session’s virtual API. allow-dns-egress External egress, vCluster, or Data is enabled Cluster DNS. allow-external-egress External egress is enabled and external CIDRs are set The configured external CIDRs, with exclusions. allow-internal-egress Valid network.internalEgress entries exist Selected Pods and ports in other namespaces.

The per-Datalab spec.security.externalEgress setting overrides the environment default. An empty external CIDR list creates no broad external allow rule.

Set the cluster Service and Pod CIDRs and any blocked ranges in the EnvironmentConfig. The provider excludes them from broad external rules. Use network.internalEgress for selected storage, identity, and other platform services.

network.excludePolicies can omit generated policies by name. Data services also have their own policies. Check the policies actually installed in each namespace when testing a connection.

docs.title: Data and public routes
docs.text:
spec.data.enabled defaults to true and cannot change after Datalab creation. Set it when creating the resource. spec.data.readOnlyMount controls Data browser permissions; storage IAM still controls object access. The optional Data S3 endpoint is always read only.

Manage public routes in the host cluster. For a permanent Data address, the public load balancer must reach the selected Gateway listener, and that listener must terminate TLS. Storage can be ready before the Data workload and its route are ready.

See installation for routing values and IAM integration for authentication.

docs.title: Persistent data
docs.text: Session files use PVCs; datasets use object storage; managed stores have their own volumes. Stopping a session keeps its home volume. See Operations for backups, retention, host security, and platform recovery.

docs.title: Install and configure Workspace
docs.text: Install the runtime, provider dependencies, composition packages, and API in that order. Use your platform’s GitOps process for a shared cluster.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
The platform needs Crossplane v2, Keycloak, object storage, an ingress controller, and a network plugin that enforces NetworkPolicy. Install the providers, functions, namespaced ProviderConfigs, and RBAC required by the selected Storage and Datalab packages.

Install Educates before creating Datalabs. The selected Educates base or ingress policies can also require Kyverno. Provider Datalab passes security settings to Educates; it does not create a complete host security policy.

Optional PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Qdrant stores need their operators installed first. The Provider Datalab installation guide lists these dependencies.

docs.title: Charts and API
docs.text:
This repository publishes charts in GitHub Packages:

Component What it installs Educates dependency chart The session runtime. Its input is dependencies/input.yaml. workspace-pipeline The Storage and Datalab configuration packages and one EnvironmentConfig.

Deploy the Workspace API and UI separately. Their source repository describes API configuration.

The pipeline uses skipDependencyResolution: true. It does not install the packages’ providers or functions. Check the exact package pins in pipeline/values.yaml; set storage.package and datalab.package to change them. A deployed environment can use different pins from this checkout.

From this checkout, save the values below as workspace-values.yaml, replace the example domains and network ranges, then install the pipeline:

helm upgrade --install workspace-pipeline ./pipeline \
  --namespace workspace --create-namespace \
  --values workspace-values.yaml

Check package health before creating a workspace:

kubectl get configurations.pkg.crossplane.io
kubectl get providers.pkg.crossplane.io
kubectl get functions.pkg.crossplane.io

docs.title: Educates runtime values
docs.text:
These values configure the Educates dependency chart, rather than the pipeline chart. Use the same domain, ingress class, and certificate in the Datalab environment configuration.

Key Purpose clusterIngressDomain Session domain, such as lab.example.org. clusterIngressClass Session ingress controller, such as apisix or nginx. tlsCertificateRef.name TLS Secret used for session hosts. tlsCertificateRef.namespace Namespace containing that TLS Secret.

docs.title: Pipeline environment values
docs.text: The keys below are under environmentconfig in Helm values. The chart writes them into EnvironmentConfig.data. Empty default fields leave the provider to choose its fallback. The Datalab resource can override session resource and security defaults.

docs.title: Identity and routing
docs.text:
Key Purpose name EnvironmentConfig name. Chart default: datalab. iam.realm Keycloak realm. iam.namespace Keycloak namespace. iam.issuerURL Public realm URL used for login. iam.internalURL Realm URL reachable from the cluster. iam.extraAudiences Extra audiences for generated workspace-client tokens, such as workspace-api. ingress.enabled Use an Ingress for permanent Data access. Chart default: false. ingress.class, ingress.domain, ingress.secret Ingress controller, workspace domain, and TLS Secret name. The domain is also used by Data HTTPRoutes. ingress.annotations Ingress controller settings. httpRoute.enabled Use Gateway API for permanent Data access. Chart default: true. httpRoute.enableS3 Enable experimental S3 reads. Chart default: false. Requires HTTPRoute access. httpRoute.parentName, httpRoute.parentNamespace Gateway name and namespace. httpRoute.sectionName HTTPS listener that terminates TLS for Data. httpRoute.httpSectionName HTTP listener for the HTTPS redirect route.

For a permanent Data address, enable exactly one of ingress.enabled and httpRoute.enabled. With both disabled, Data uses session ingress. Enabling both stops reconciliation. The public load balancer must send traffic to the selected controller or Gateway.

docs.title: Storage and services
docs.text: Key Purpose storage.endpoint, storage.region Backing S3 endpoint and region. storage.forcePathStyle Path-style S3 addresses. Chart default: true; written as a string for the provider. storage.provider, storage.type Storage provider label and type. Type defaults to s3. storage.secretNamespace Namespace where Datalabs read their input storage Secrets. storage.lifecycle.schedule Storage lifecycle-job cron schedule. Provider fallback: 17 2 * * *. storageClasses.allowed Session PVC classes. An unlisted requested class falls back to the first entry. An empty list allows the requested or cluster default class. database.storageClassName, database.backupStorageClassName PostgreSQL data and backup classes, where supported by its operator. database.tlsRoute.parentName, database.tlsRoute.parentNamespace, database.tlsRoute.sectionName Gateway listener for optional external PostgreSQL access. mongodb.storageClassName, redis.storageClassName, qdrant.storageClassName Managed-store volume classes. Empty uses the cluster default. packages Extension packages for sessions.

docs.title: Resources and network
docs.text:
Key Purpose defaults.quota.memory Session memory. Provider fallback: 2Gi. defaults.quota.storage Session home-volume size. Provider fallback: 1Gi. defaults.quota.budget Educates resource budget. Provider fallback: medium. defaults.overallQuota.storage Total PVC requests in the Datalab environment namespace. Provider fallback: 100Gi. defaults.security.policy Pod security level: restricted, baseline, or privileged. Provider fallback: baseline. defaults.security.kubernetesAccess Supply a Kubernetes service account token. Provider fallback: true. defaults.security.kubernetesRole Namespace role: view, edit, or admin. Provider fallback: edit. defaults.security.externalEgress Enable the configured external rules. Provider fallback: true. network.externalEgressCIDRs External ranges allowed when external egress is enabled. An empty list creates no broad external allow rule. network.internalEgress Allowed namespaces, Pod selectors, and ports for internal services. network.serviceCIDR, network.podCIDRs Cluster address ranges excluded from broad external rules. network.blacklistIPs Other ranges excluded from broad external rules, such as metadata endpoints. network.excludePolicies Generated NetworkPolicy names to omit.

See operational controls for how these settings affect sessions and Data.

docs.title: Example values
docs.text:
This example uses Gateway API for Data. Its HTTPS listener needs a certificate for *.lab.example.org and must accept routes from Datalab runtime namespaces. S3 reads also need support for HTTPRoute header regular expressions.

environmentconfig:
  name: datalab
  iam:
    realm: eoepca
    namespace: iam
    issuerURL: https://identity.example.org/realms/eoepca
    internalURL: http://keycloak-service.iam.svc/realms/eoepca
    extraAudiences:
      - workspace-api
  ingress:
    enabled: false
    class: apisix
    domain: lab.example.org
    secret: workspace-tls
  httpRoute:
    enabled: true
    enableS3: true
    parentName: public
    parentNamespace: gateway
    sectionName: workspaces-https
    httpSectionName: http
  storage:
    endpoint: https://s3.example.org
    forcePathStyle: true
    provider: Other
    region: us-east-1
    secretNamespace: workspace
    type: s3
  network:
    externalEgressCIDRs:
      - 0.0.0.0/0
      - ::/0
    internalEgress:
      - namespace: platform-services
        podSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: artifact-proxy
        ports:
          - protocol: TCP
            port: 443
    serviceCIDR: 10.43.0.0/16
    podCIDRs:
      - 10.42.0.0/16
    blacklistIPs:
      - 169.254.169.254/32
      - fd00:ec2::254/128
  defaults:
    overallQuota:
      storage: 100Gi
    security:
      policy: baseline
      kubernetesAccess: true
      kubernetesRole: edit
      externalEgress: true

httpRoute.enableS3 applies to all Data-enabled Datalabs in this environment. There is no per-Datalab S3 override. It controls the read-only Data endpoint; backing storage retains its own permissions.

For external PostgreSQL, configure a separate TLS-passthrough listener through database.tlsRoute. The Gateway controller must serve TLSRoute v1 and support direct PostgreSQL TLS with SNI.

docs.title: Select the environment
docs.text:
The chart creates one EnvironmentConfig named datalab by default. A manually created Storage resource can select it with:

metadata:
  labels:
    storages.pkg.internal/environment: datalab

Without an environment annotation or label, the MinIO composition selects storage. The Datalab key is datalabs.pkg.internal/environment. The Workspace API uses its PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT setting for resources it creates; its default is datalab.

docs.title: Verify the user path
docs.text: Create a test workspace with Workspace Management. Check storage and Data separately, then run Vienna for public and S3 downloads. Use STAC registration to check the session registry and vCluster.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Create a test workspace, publish images, and serve STAC metadata. Use the same workspace for all three notebooks.

docs.title: Environment assumptions
docs.text:
These examples use eoepca-demo. The repository includes public service settings in eoepca-demo.env and a three-Item sample in docs/catalog.v1.parquet.

Requirement Used for alice and oscar accounts Alice owns the workspace; Oscar has the workspace-api platform admin role and creates it. Storage and a permanent Data address Upload files, browse public shares, and download data. Data S3 endpoint enabled Run the authenticated S3 and AWS CLI steps. Datalab with vCluster and registry Run the STAC registration notebook.

An operator sets up the accounts and roles and installs Workspace. For another deployment, change the service settings and account names.

docs.title: 1. Create a workspace
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/workspace-management.ipynb

Run Workspace Management. Sign in as Alice with device login, then as Oscar when the notebook asks for an administrator.

The notebook creates ws-test-<UTC timestamp>, waits for storage, and refreshes Alice’s token to load her workspace roles. Copy the printed workspace name for the other notebooks.

The API returns a name, for example:

{"name": "ws-test-20261024071434"}

The dashboard address is WORKSPACE_API_ENDPOINT/<workspace-name>. The API adds the configured ws- prefix to the preferred name.

docs.title: 2. Open the workspace
docs.text:
Open the dashboard link as Alice. It shows the storage connection and available sessions. Open a Datalab session to use its editor, terminal, and Data tab.

In on-demand mode, opening a stopped session starts it. Storage and the permanent Data service can be available before the session starts. The notebook waits separately for storage and the public Data route.

Use Management → Sessions to check the default session:

Workspace Management uploads the sample catalogue and six preview images. It checks each image through an expiring S3 link, then through a permanent public-share link. Both downloads must match the uploaded bytes.

docs.title: 3. Publish and read satellite images
docs.text:
Open Vienna imagery with STAC and S3 and enter the workspace name from step 1.

The notebook:

  1. Crops three Sentinel-2 images over Vienna and creates previews.
  2. Uploads those files and a STAC GeoParquet catalogue.
  3. Reads the published STAC items and public image links.
  4. Uses device login for authenticated S3 reads and the AWS CLI.
  5. Checks a byte-range read and compares download checksums.

Existing objects with matching checksums are kept. A different file at the same key stops the upload.

Open /share/public/ on the Data hostname to browse the published files:

docs.title: 4. Register metadata without copying the rasters
docs.text:
Start the workspace’s default Datalab session. Open Register STAC metadata in that session and set its workspace name as described there.

The notebook selects three STAC items from DLR’s Geoservice, builds an OCI metadata package, and starts a STAC API in the session’s vCluster. It checks the package after each transfer. The raster files remain at the source.

The notebooks leave the workspace, uploaded files, and OCI package available for inspection.

docs.title: 5. Work with a team
docs.text:
Use the management page to add members and manage bucket access. Members use the workspace’s storage identity. To use a bucket owned by another workspace, request access and have its owner approve the grant.

See Concepts for the access model and steps for managing members, bucket grants, and sessions.

docs.title: 6. Use managed services
docs.text:
A workspace can request PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, or Qdrant when the platform has the required operators. Use the Stores tab when these services are available. Their connection settings appear on the dashboard and in new Datalab sessions.

For operator configuration and application examples, see Add a managed service.

docs.title: Register STAC metadata¶
docs.text:
Select three STAC items from DLR's Geoservice, publish them as an OCI package, and serve them from a workspace STAC API. Clients can query the selected items while the raster files remain at the source.

The notebook checks package file hashes after registry transfer and deployment. It also checks the API items, source geometry, and asset URLs.

Create a workspace with Workspace Management first. Use Vienna imagery when you want to copy image files into workspace storage too.

docs.title: 1. Configure the workspace¶
docs.text:
Use the test workspace created with Workspace Management. Start its default Datalab session from the workspace dashboard and run this notebook there.

The session supplies KUBECONFIG, REGISTRY_HOST, REGISTRY_USERNAME, and REGISTRY_PASSWORD. Set EOEPCA_WORKSPACE to the test workspace name and EOEPCA_SESSION=default before starting Jupyter. For a local kernel, supply the same settings and a kubeconfig for that session's vCluster.

Registry access uses its supplied Basic credentials. These credentials are separate from user device login.

From the repository checkout, install the dependencies and start Jupyter:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/getting-started/register-stac-metadata.ipynb

Command, retry, and checksum functions are in the shared notebook helper.

docs.title: 2. Select STAC Items¶
docs.text:
The collection on DLR's Geoservice has global daily rasters. The bounding box selects intersecting Items; it does not crop the images. Keep each Item's original geometry and projection fields.

STAC time searches also match intersecting intervals. A 31 July Item can match an August search if its interval crosses midnight. Filter on the Item's representative datetime to select the three days used here.

docs.title: 3. Build the package¶
docs.text:
Build from the selected Items. The package contains:

  • items.parquet: the STAC items as GeoParquet.
  • assets.lock.parquet: source asset URLs and available object metadata.
  • collections.json: the API collection document, pointing to items.parquet.

--no-probe-metadata skips requests for source object headers. The source files are not copied.

docs.title: 4. Publish to the OCI registry¶
docs.text: Push the package to the session registry. The tag includes part of the Item-table checksum so it is easier to identify.

docs.title: Check the published package¶
docs.text:
Tags can be reassigned. Resolve the tag to a manifest digest and pull by that digest. Compare each downloaded file's SHA-256 with its value before the push.

This checks the metadata package, not the raster files at the source URLs. It does not authenticate the publisher.

docs.title: 5. Start the STAC API¶
docs.text:
Apply the manifests in register-stac-metadata/ to the vCluster. The init container uses the cng-stac-api-registry Secret to pull the package into an emptyDir volume. The API then reads /data/collections.json and /data/items.parquet from that volume.

Other workloads in the vCluster can reach it at:

http://cng-stac-api.default.svc.cluster.local

After rollout, compare the checksums inside the API container with the original package files.

docs.title: 6. Query the API¶
docs.text:
Use a port-forward to reach the internal Service from the notebook. The cell checks the API and prints browser links through the editor proxy at /proxy/<port>/.

Use those printed URLs: links returned by the API omit the proxy prefix. Keep the Jupyter kernel running while using the browser links. Workloads in the vCluster can use the Service URL directly.

docs.title: 7. Keep or remove the demo API¶
docs.text:
By default, the API remains available in the vCluster and the OCI package stays in the registry. The local port-forward lasts while the notebook kernel is running.

Set EOEPCA_CLEAN_UP=1 to remove the API workload, Service, init script, and registry Secret. The package remains in the registry.

docs.title: Result and next step¶
docs.text:
The workspace now serves three selected STAC items from a package identified by its OCI digest. Their geometry and asset URLs match the source. Clients still read raster data from DLR's Geoservice.

To keep image files in workspace storage, copy them, check their hashes, and update the STAC asset links. The Vienna notebook shows image preparation and upload.

def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()

docs.title: Vienna imagery with STAC and S3¶
docs.text:
Publish three Sentinel-2 image crops and their STAC items in one workspace. Read the images through public STAC links and authenticated S3 clients, and check that both routes return the uploaded bytes.

First create a workspace with Workspace Management. Use its printed name below. Files uploaded under public/ are publicly readable.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the runtime¶
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/getting-started/vienna-imagery-with-stac-and-s3.ipynb

The notebook uses eoepca-demo.env for service settings. Sign in as the test workspace owner with device login when prompted. Storage keys and tokens stay in kernel memory.

Install the AWS CLI for step 8 if your runtime does not already provide it.

docs.title: 2. Select the scenes¶
docs.text:
Use three fixed scene IDs from February, May, and August. The reported cloud cover applies to each source tile. It can differ from the cloud cover over Vienna.

Crop each image to the Vienna bounding box and write a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF with a PNG preview. Keep the cropped grid in the STAC metadata. The August scene uses a different tile, so its available crop differs.

docs.title: 3. Write the STAC catalogue¶
docs.text:
The public share reads public/catalog.parquet. Asset paths must be relative to public, such as vienna-s2l2a-26/<scene-id>/overview.tif. PackageR turns those paths into public download links in returned STAC Items.

The catalogue records the source scene links, license, and cropped grid. It contains colour imagery and previews; use the original reflectance bands for numerical analysis.

docs.title: 4. Upload to the bucket¶
docs.text:
Sign in as the workspace owner. The Workspace API supplies its backing storage credentials. The Data S3 endpoint used later is read only.

Check existing files by SHA-256. Skip matching files and stop if a key has different content. Upload the catalogue after its assets.

docs.title: 5. Browse STAC and download an image¶
docs.text:
The public share reads public/catalog.parquet. Follow its Item links to the images. This catalogue has no /search endpoint.

The cells check the three STAC items, download a COG and preview, and compare their checksums with the local files.

docs.title: Browse the dynamic STAC API¶
docs.text:
PackageR builds a dynamic STAC API from the uploaded STAC GeoParquet file at /api/public/catalog/public. The API serves the Collection and its items without a separate STAC server deployment.

Open it in STAC Browser to view the three scenes on a map and browse their image assets. The link and embedded page below use the workspace selected in step 1. If your notebook viewer blocks the embedded page, use the link.

docs.title: 6. Use device login for S3¶
docs.text:
Refresh the owner's login. The token needs the workspace audience and workspace access role. Use the workspace name for both S3 signing names and the access token as the session token.

If the login expired, run the sign-in cell in step 4 again.

docs.title: 7. Read through S3¶
docs.text: List the published files, inspect an object, check a byte-range GET, and download all seven files. Compare each downloaded file with its local SHA-256 checksum.

docs.title: 8. Download with the AWS CLI¶
docs.text: Use aws s3 ls to list the images and aws s3 cp to download one. The helper uses the device login and a temporary CLI configuration.

docs.title: Result¶
docs.text: The workspace holds three COG images, three PNG previews, and one catalogue. The public image and preview downloads, all seven S3 downloads, and the CLI image download match the local SHA-256 checksums. A byte-range request returns the requested part of an image.

docs.title: Notebook guide
docs.text:
The notebooks cover three parts of a workspace workflow. Start with Workspace Management and use its printed workspace name in the other two.

Notebook What it demonstrates What the checks prove Workspace Management An administrator creates storage for a user; the user uploads and shares files. Storage is ready, the owner’s roles are available, and temporary and public downloads match the uploaded images. Vienna imagery with STAC and S3 Publish image files and their STAC metadata in one workspace. Read them with public links and authenticated S3 clients. The three STAC items describe the cropped images; public, S3, and AWS CLI downloads have matching checksums. Byte-range reads return the requested bytes. Register STAC metadata Package STAC items from DLR’s Geoservice once, then serve them from a workspace STAC API. The OCI package survives push, pull, and deployment with the same file checksums. API queries return the selected items and their source asset links.

docs.title: Choose where to run
docs.text:
Run Workspace Management and Vienna from this repository with uv sync and uv run jupyter lab. They read public service settings from eoepca-demo.env and use device login for user access. Install the AWS CLI for Vienna’s final step.

Run STAC registration in the test workspace’s Datalab. It needs the session registry credentials and vCluster kubeconfig supplied by that runtime. Its OCI registry login uses Basic authentication.

docs.title: Choose what to publish
docs.text:
Use Vienna when you want the image files in workspace storage. Its public catalogue serves Collection and Item links.

Use registration when the source already hosts the rasters and you want a selected metadata package with a fixed OCI digest. Its deployed API also supports STAC search. Access to the raster files still depends on the source service.

The quickstart gives the run order and prerequisites. Each notebook keeps its outputs so you can inspect the images, checksums, and API results.
